areas.area: Core architecture and rule registry (src/quality/compliance: mod.rs, context.rs, registry.rs, shared.rs + consumers in src/quality/scorer.rs, src/cli/{quality,validate}.rs, src/reports)
areas.summary: The core is well-designed post-fixes: a read-only ComplianceContext + StandardChecker trait dispatch (checker_for) cleanly splits 16 levels across 9 dedicated checkers and a generic path, and the rule registry (registry.rs::rule_meta) is a genuine single source of truth for SARIF IDs, standard cross-references, and remediation, back-filled centrally in ComplianceChecker::check(). Every rule_id emitted from src/quality/compliance/* resolves in the registry, and there are no panics/unwraps reachable from untrusted SBOM input. The main defects are at the seams: the `validate` CLI ships parallel hand-rolled NTIA/FDA checkers that reach different verdicts than the engine for the same standard (false-pass), the dedicated-checker dispatch creates coverage holes because dedicated profiles skip the generic checks entirely (BSI misses the mandatory component-version element; engine NTIA misses unique identifiers), and three separate SARIF rule-ID surfaces (registry sarif_id, hand-maintained rule tables, quality CLI's invented QUALITY-* IDs) have drifted apart. The JSON contract also omits the stable rule key entirely (serde-skipped), undermining the registry's purpose for machine consumers. Extensibility cost of a new framework is ~8-10 edit sites across 6 files with only one weak test guarding consistency.
strengths: Rule registry design: Violation.rule_id -> rule_meta() is the single source for SARIF IDs, harmonised-standard refs, and remediation; check() back-fills standard_refs centrally so rewording a message cannot drop a prEN/BSI reference (mod.rs:858-865, registry.rs:52-59).

StandardChecker dispatch is clean and cheap: read-only ComplianceContext, dedicated_checker! macro eliminates boilerplate, checker_for() is exhaustive over dedicated levels with a generic fallback, and a debug_assert verifies dispatched level matches configuration (context.rs:96-155, mod.rs:853-857).

No panics/unwraps on untrusted SBOM input anywhere in the check paths; the only expect() is on a hard-coded RFC-3339 literal (cra.rs:705); arithmetic uses saturating_sub and .max(1) denominators; the epoch-sentinel timestamp handling (has_known_timestamp) avoids bogus ~20000-day ages.
Severity calibration is centralized: class_severity()/vendor_hash_threshold() encode the CRA product-class table in one place instead of scattering per-check ladders (mod.rs:763-825).

Recent fixes hold up: crypto vacuous-pass gates (SBOM-CNSA2-000/SBOM-PQC-000), NTIA timestamp/supplier gating, deterministic Art.14 tests via check_article_14_readiness_at(now, ...) injection, and the ComplianceResult counts are consistent with is_compliant (mod.rs:613-639).

Good test hygiene at the core: registry-ref tests, sidecar precedence tests, mocked-clock Art.14 tests, and a per-module BSIAI test asserting all emitted rule IDs are registered and prefixed (bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs:838-857).

areas.area: EU CRA profiles (src/quality/compliance/cra.rs, CraPhase/CraOssSteward in mod.rs, src/cli/cra_docs.rs)
areas.summary: The CRA engine is well-structured (sidecar fallback design, class-calibrated severities, clock-injectable Art. 14 checks, registry-driven standard refs) but has two verdict-level defects confirmed end-to-end with the built binary: the CraOssSteward profile's "SBOM completeness" gate is vacuous because check_components/check_dependencies match on level lists that exclude CraOssSteward (a version-less, identifier-less, edge-less SBOM passes as compliant), and pinning an explicit product class (even a stricter one, important-1) downgrades the Phase2 vendor-hash <50% Error to a Warning, flipping non-compliant to compliant. The regulatory metadata layer has systematic citation errors verified against Reg. (EU) 2024/2847: the phase model asserts deadlines (reporting 2027-12-11, full compliance 2029-12-11) that contradict Art. 71 (Art. 14 reporting from 2026-09-11 — which cra.rs itself hard-codes correctly — and full application 2027-12-11; no 2029 milestone exists), and violations/SARIF/dossiers cite nonexistent "Annex I Part III", label the important-products list (Annex III) as document integrity, and swap Annex V (EU DoC) with Annex VII (technical documentation). Several presence heuristics pass vacuously: any third-party component's upstream advisories/support external refs satisfy the manufacturer's Art. 13(6) security-contact and Art. 13(7) CVD-policy checks. Phase gating is otherwise coherent, but CraPhase1 is unreachable from any CLI path (validate/quality/reports all hard-code CraPhase2).
strengths: Art. 14 readiness check uses the correct 2026-09-11 deadline from Art. 71(2), takes an injectable clock (check_article_14_readiness_at) for deterministic tests, splits pre-deadline Info vs post-deadline Warning/Error, and escalates severity by product class (cra.rs:695-795).

Sidecar design is sound: SBOM fields always win, sidecar downgrades missing-field Warnings to Info instead of silently suppressing (Art. 13(6)/(12)/(15)/13(7) paths in generic.rs), auto-discovery handles multi-extension stems, and CLI-vs-sidecar product-class mismatches are logged (validate.rs:57-65).

Product-class -> conformity-route defaults match Art. 32 (Default/Important-1 -> Module A, Important-2 -> Module B+C, Critical -> EUCC) and the class-severity calibration table is centralized and unit-tested (mod.rs:763-812, tests/cra_product_class_tests.rs).
Rule registry decouples SARIF IDs, standard refs, and remediation from message text, with an exhaustive no-orphan-rule test (mod.rs every_emitted_violation_has_a_registered_rule_id).

Hardware [PRE-8-RQ-02] checks are non-vacuous (silent only when no hardware components exist) and require producer, real identifier, and firmware version with a device->firmware graph fallback (cra.rs:805-905).

areas.area: AI-BOM compliance profiles (EU AI Act Annex IV + BSI/G7 SBOM-for-AI)
areas.summary: The two AI-BOM profiles are well-framed (explicit READINESS language, N/A gating, MUST/SHOULD/Info severity calibration, registered rule IDs with SARIF/remediation metadata) and read both CycloneDX 1.5+ modelCard/data components and SPDX 3.0 AI/Dataset profiles through one normalized model. However, the N/A gate leaks in both directions — execution-verified: a plain web-app SBOM containing one generic `data` component (config bundle) is judged NON-COMPLIANT under BSI-AI (exit 1) because every Data component is treated as an AI dataset, while an SBOM whose model carries a full CycloneDX modelCard but is typed `application` gets "Not applicable"/compliant from both profiles because the ML filter keys only on component_type and ignores ml_model presence. A CDX model documented via a `model-card` external reference (without a modelCard object) is flagged as lacking a model card/description, which becomes blocking Errors under the high-risk sidecar flag. Finally, N/A results are indistinguishable from genuine passes in machine-readable output ({"compliant":true,"score":100}). The gating/filter logic and N/A boilerplate are duplicated verbatim across the two modules, so fixes must land in two places.
strengths: N/A gating exists and is honestly worded: non-AI SBOMs get a single Info finding with an explicit 'readiness profile, not a legal-conformity guarantee' disclaimer, and level names/descriptions repeat the READINESS framing (mod.rs:96-113, 136-137, 200-205), so report wording does not overclaim legal compliance in prose

Dual-format coverage is real: CycloneDX 1.5+ modelCard/considerations/quantitativeAnalysis and component.data are parsed (cyclonedx.rs:523-630) and SPDX 3.0 AI/Dataset profile fields (ai_metric, ai_limitation, ai_energyConsumption, dataset_intendedUse, dataset_confidentialityLevel, TRAINED_ON relationships) are normalized into the same MlModelInfo/DatasetInfo (spdx3.rs:555-686), keeping both checkers format-agnostic

Severity is calibrated to normative language (BSI MUST=Error, SHOULD=Warning, unmodeled elements=Info placeholders so the scorecard stays complete; EU-AI-Act gaps are Warnings that escalate to Errors under the sidecar isHighRiskAi flag) — escalation verified end-to-end via --cra-sidecar

Rule hygiene: every emitted rule_id is registered with SARIF id, remediation text, and standard refs; unit tests enforce registration and prefix conventions, and integration tests (tests/eu_ai_act_tests.rs, tests/bsi_sbom_for_ai_tests.rs) cover fixtures, CLI paths, and SARIF emission including help URIs (sarif.rs:738-741)

areas.area: Integration, CLI surface, and report rendering (compliance engine)

The biggest remaining defect is that `validate --standard ntia` uses a hand-rolled checker that diverges from the engine's NtiaMinimum (no timestamp check, required elements downgraded to warnings), producing false COMPLIANT verdicts. Renderer-level distortions cluster around SARIF (duplicate rule descriptors in multi-standard runs, CNSA2/PQC results with no rule metadata, the quality command's hand-rolled SARIF ignoring the registry entirely) and around silent format fallbacks (oscal-json silently becoming plain JSON for diff/view, quality/validate silently emitting text for html/markdown). Multi-standard validate runs work in one invocation (comma-separated), output order is stable (CLI order) across text/JSON/SARIF/OSCAL, and exit-code aggregation (1=any errors, 2=warnings with --fail-on-warning) matches the single-standard contract

Exit codes are centrally defined with documented per-command aliases whose numeric stability is test-enforced (pipeline/mod.rs exit_codes), and --fail-on-noncompliant (3f996e5) is correctly opt-in so existing --min-score pipelines are unaffected

SARIF helpUri wrapping (SarifRuleWithUri) derives canonical regulation URLs at serialization time and is covered by tests/sarif_help_uri_tests.rs for CRA/BSI; result-level standardHelpUris parallel standardIds

areas.area: Test coverage assessment — SBOM compliance engine (src/quality/compliance/, CLI + report surfaces)
areas.summary: Coverage is heavily skewed toward the CRA family and the two AI readiness profiles: CraPhase2 (9 test files, sidecar precedence, product-class severity table pinned row-by-row, mocked-clock Art. 14), CraOssSteward, EuccSubstantial, EuAiAct and BsiSbomForAi all have real pass AND fail verdict assertions. At the other extreme, FdaMedicalDevice, Standard, and Comprehensive have zero behavioral tests anywhere (they are only swept by the no-orphan registry loops, which assert rule registration, not verdicts), Minimum has one incidental false-positive test, and NistSsdf/Eo14028 each have exactly one rule with a behavioral assertion and no passing-case test at all — a checker that always errors (or one whose non-tested rules are deleted) would keep the suite green. Crypto profiles are mid-tier: CNSA2 has a genuine compliant-fixture pass test, but ALG-004/ALG-007/CERT-001 and the PQC ECB/key-size/missing-level rules are never individually asserted and the fixture tests use aggregate ">=5 errors" assertions that hide single-rule regressions; NistPqc has no pass-verdict test even though a quantum-ready fixture exists. The recently added `quality --fail-on-noncompliant` exit gate (commit 3f996e5) shipped with no test, and the CLI `validate --standard` dispatch is untested for 8 of 12 standards including the CLI-local FDA/NTIA implementations that diverge from the engine checkers. There is no property/fuzz coverage of the compliance path (proptest_quality covers only QualityScorer), and all compliance fixtures are hand-rolled minimal CycloneDX — the one real-tool 3798-component fixture in the tree is used by no test.
strengths: CRA Phase 2 ecosystem is thoroughly tested: sidecar field precedence and downgrades (tests in src/quality/compliance/mod.rs:1350-1449), product-class severity calibration table pinned row-by-row (tests/cra_product_class_tests.rs:398-482), vendor-hash thresholds per class, conformity summary per route (tests/cra_conformity_summary_tests.rs), and both compliant and non-compliant golden fixtures (tests/cra_golden_fixtures_tests.rs).

Date-dependent CRA Art. 14 checks have an injectable-clock seam (check_article_14_readiness_at) with explicit pre/post-deadline mocked-clock tests (src/quality/compliance/mod.rs:1740-1798), avoiding wall-clock flakiness.

The four recent fix commits landed with targeted regression tests: crypto vacuous-pass (crypto_standards_fail_on_empty_inventory, pqc_flags_classical_crypto_with_unset_quantum_level, cnsa2_flags_weak_sha2_in_either_encoding at src/quality/compliance/mod.rs:1133-1209) and required-element gates (ntia_gates_on_missing_timestamp, eo14028_gates_on_missing_supplier, bsi_gates_on_nameless_component, cra_art24_honors_document_level_disclosure at mod.rs:890-982).

SARIF external rule-ID stability is pinned (tests/compliance_rule_registry_tests.rs:136-173) protecting GitHub code-scanning dedup, and the no-orphan-rule invariant runs across all 16 ComplianceLevel variants against a representative fixture set.

Both AI readiness profiles (EuAiAct, BsiSbomForAi) test the full verdict matrix: fully-documented pass, sparse fail with specific rule_ids, non-AI N/A gate that never fails, high-risk sidecar escalation, SARIF rule emission, and (for BSI-AI) the CLI path with exit codes (tests/eu_ai_act_tests.rs, tests/bsi_sbom_for_ai_tests.rs, plus src #[cfg(test)] blocks).

EUCC Substantial covers all four must-have references, expired vs near-expiry certificate semantics using relative dates (not fragile absolute dates), and controls-assertion evidence handling (tests/cra_p5_tests.rs).

Golden report snapshots exist for all 10 diff-report formats with disciplined volatile-field redaction, plus SARIF structural invariants (every result references a declared rule) in tests/golden_reports.rs:309-347.

confirmed.description: Engine NtiaMinimum (generic.rs path, emits SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP/VERSION/... ) and the CLI-local check_ntia_compliance (validate.rs:329, emits SBOM-NTIA-AUTHOR/NAME/VERSION/SUPPLIER/IDENTIFIER/DEPENDENCY, and has NO timestamp rule) are separate rule sets. Unit tests (mod.rs:890-921) cover the engine's timestamp gate; CLI exit-code tests (cli_contract_tests.rs:29-65) cover the CLI-local implementation, rule-blind. No test asserts the two paths agree on a verdict for the same SBOM, so the 3f996e5 timestamp-gate fix is only enforced on the engine path — `validate --standard ntia` still passes a timestamp-less SBOM and no test documents or guards that asymmetry.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A timestamp-less SBOM: `ComplianceChecker::new(NtiaMinimum).check()` returns non-compliant (Error), while `sbom-tools validate --standard ntia` exits 0 — contradictory NTIA verdicts from the same binary. Both test suites pass, so the divergence can widen indefinitely with every one-sided rule change.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: Confirmed on all points, and the divergence is even wider than claimed. (1) Two implementations exist: `validate --standard ntia` dispatches to CLI-local check_ntia_compliance (src/cli/validate.rs:73, defined at :329-410), which emits SBOM-NTIA-AUTHOR/NAME/VERSION/SUPPLIER/IDENTIFIER/DEPENDENCY and has NO timestamp rule; the engine's NtiaMinimum path (src/quality/compliance/generic.rs:395-410) emits SBOM-NTIA-TIMESTAMP as a gating Error (the 3f996e5 fix touched only this path). (2) The engine path IS reachable from the same binary: `quality --profile security` maps to ComplianceLevel::NtiaMini

confirmed.title: EuAiAct rules 2D-SENSITIVITY and 2G-ENERGY have no firing/suppression assertions
confirmed.description: SBOM-AIACT-ANNEX-IV-2D-SENSITIVITY (eu_ai_act.rs:217) and SBOM-AIACT-ANNEX-IV-2G-ENERGY (eu_ai_act.rs:406) are only touched by all_emitted_rule_ids_are_registered (registration check). Neither the bare-model negative test (eu_ai_act.rs:507-518) nor the fixture tests assert these rules fire on missing sensitivity classification / energy disclosure or stay silent when present (full_ml_component sets energy_kwh_training but no test asserts the absence of 2G-ENERGY specifically).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The energy-disclosure condition regresses to never fire (or always fire); Annex IV §2(g) energy readiness silently disappears from (or floods) reports and only the aggregate warning_count==0 assertion in fully_documented_ai_sbom_has_no_readiness_warnings could catch one direction.

confirmed.title: BSI-AI System-Level, Infrastructure, and Security cluster elements lack per-element verdict tests
confirmed.description: The Models/Datasets clusters have both pass and fail assertions, but the SYS-PRIMARY/SYS-PRODUCER/SYS-DATAFLOW (check_bsiai_system_level_cluster, bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs:171), INFRA-RUNTIME (:516), SEC-CONTROLS/SEC-EXPLOITABILITY (:557), and META-FORMAT/TIMESTAMP/TOOL/SIGNATURE elements are only swept by the rule-registration loop (bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs:838-860) and by broad ids.contains checks for META-AUTHOR. No test asserts, e.g., that a missing primary component fires SYS-PRIMARY or that a runtime edge suppresses INFRA-RUNTIME (the pass-case adds an edge but never asserts INFRA-RUNTIME's absence by id).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The system-level primary-component condition inverts; every AI-BOM gains (or loses) SYS-PRIMARY findings. The pass-case test only asserts a fixed list of MODEL-*/DATASET-* ids and is_compliant, so an Info/Warning-severity cluster regression is invisible.

confirmed.title: Golden JSON snapshots redact warning_count/info_count globally, blinding them to count regressions everywhere
confirmed.description: To absorb the CRA Art. 14 deadline flip, redacted_settings() replaces every `"warning_count": N` and `"info_count": N` in the entire JSON/streaming/NDJSON output (tests/golden_reports.rs:113-114), not just within the CRA block. Combined with the severity redaction at :106-109, the golden baselines can no longer detect a report-wide regression in violation counting or Art.14-adjacent severity assignment; the redaction scope is much broader than the volatility it targets.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A reporter bug doubles warning_count in the JSON diff report (e.g. counting per-standard-ref instead of per-violation); all golden snapshots still match because every count is [N], and no other test asserts those serialized counts.

improvements.title: Registry-driven per-rule test matrix (every rule id gets a firing + silent case)
improvements.description: The rule registry (src/quality/compliance/registry.rs) already enumerates all ~100 rule ids. Add a table-driven test harness mapping each rule_id to (a) a minimal SBOM/sidecar that must fire it and (b) a minimal one that must not, then add a meta-test that fails when a registered rule has no entry. This converts the current 'no orphan rule ids' invariant into 'no untested rules' and would have surfaced every per-rule gap listed in findings (FDA, SSDF, EO14028, CNSA2 ALG-004/007/CERT-001, PQC-008/012/KEY-001, BSI 5-2/5-5) mechanically.

improvements.title: Property-based coverage of the compliance path
improvements.description: tests/proptest_quality.rs only exercises QualityScorer. Add a proptest that runs ComplianceChecker::check for every ComplianceLevel::all() over arbitrary NormalizedSboms (reusing arb_component plus optional crypto/ml strategies) asserting structural invariants: no panic, error/warning/info counts equal the violation partition, is_compliant == (error_count == 0), every rule_id resolves in rule_meta, N/A profiles (EuAiAct, BsiSbomForAi) never emit Errors for SBOMs without AI content, and monotonicity-style checks (adding a hash never increases BSI §5.4 violations).

improvements.title: Use realistic and cross-format fixtures for compliance verdicts
improvements.description: All compliance fixtures are hand-rolled minimal CycloneDX JSON; the only real-tool output in the tree (tests/fixtures/cyclonedx/sbom-cyclone-dx-json-01-kef-...json, 3798 components) is used by no test at all, and SPDX appears in the compliance suite only as minimal.spdx.json inside the registry loop. Run the big real-tool fixture and at least one real SPDX 2.3 document through the CRA/BSI/NTIA checkers with pinned verdict expectations, so format-specific normalization gaps (e.g. SPDX supplier/hash mapping) can't silently skew verdicts that are only ever tested against synthetic CycloneDX.

improvements.title: Golden snapshots for compliance report rendering (validate output), including multi-standard SARIF
improvements.description: golden_reports.rs snapshots only the diff-report renderers. Add insta snapshots for the validate/compliance surfaces: generate_compliance_sarif and generate_multi_compliance_sarif with 2+ standards, plus the markdown/HTML/JSON compliance summary blocks, using a fixed non-compliant fixture. This pins the externally consumed compliance schema the same way diff reports are pinned, and gives the multi-standard SARIF merge (currently zero coverage beyond one single-standard test) a baseline.

improvements.title: Extend the injectable-clock pattern beyond Art. 14 to eliminate date-based snapshot redaction
improvements.description: check_article_14_readiness_at shows the pattern; the SBOM-age (Art. 13(3)) and any future deadline checks still read the wall clock, forcing golden_reports.rs to regex-redact severities and counts (see finding on over-broad redaction). Thread a `now: DateTime<Utc>` through ComplianceChecker (defaulting to Utc::now) so goldens can pin a fixed date and drop the [ART14_SEV]/count filters, restoring snapshot sensitivity.

improvements.title: CLI standard-alias contract test
improvements.description: One table-driven CLI test iterating every documented `validate --standard` alias (ntia, fda, cra, ssdf/nist-ssdf, eo14028, cnsa2/cnsa2.0, pqc, bsi/tr-03183, oss-steward/cra-art24, eucc/common-criteria, ai-act, bsi-ai, and comma-separated combos) against one fixture, asserting exit code and that the summary names the expected profile. Cheap insurance for the 12-arm string match in src/cli/validate.rs:72-131 and for the --fail-on-noncompliant / --fail-on-warning exit-code contracts across standards.

areas.area: Ecosystem gap analysis — compliance standards coverage in src/quality/compliance/
areas.summary: Coverage is unusually deep on the EU/German axis (CRA Phase 1/2 + Art. 24 OSS steward with Annex VIII product classes/conformity routes and prEN 40000-1-3 clause mapping, BSI TR-03183-2, EUCC Substantial, EU AI Act Annex IV, BSI/G7 SBOM-for-AI) and on crypto readiness (CNSA 2.0, NIST PQC/IR 8547 over CBOM data), plus the US 2021-era baseline (NTIA, EO 14028, SSDF, FDA). The main ecosystem gaps are the US successor guidance (CISA 2025 Minimum Elements draft — already shipped as an 'ntia-2025' profile by sbomqs — and CISA's 2024 Framing/FSCT attribute tiers), industry verticals (PCI DSS 4.0 §6.3.2, mandatory since 2025-03-31; OpenChain Telco SBOM Guide), APAC (Japan METI SBOM Guide v2.0), scoring interoperability with sbomqs/BSI quality levels, and ingestion of machine-readable attestation evidence (in-toto, CycloneDX CDXA) — today conformity evidence is only detected as an ExternalRefType::Attestation presence bit. Two covered standards have version-drifted since implementation: BSI TR-03183-2 is checked against v2.0.0 while v2.1.0 (2025-08-20) is current and adds a CycloneDX>=1.6/SPDX>=3.0.1 format gate the checker never enforces, and the FDA profile predates the June 27, 2025 final premarket guidance that supersedes the Sept 2023 edition and makes SBOM statutory for cyber devices under FD&C §524B(b)(3). Almost every proposed profile can be built on data NormalizedSbom already carries (hashes, licenses, tool creators, lifecycle_phase, supplier, is_external, vulnerabilities, support_end_date), so effort is mostly rule-authoring, not model work. Sources: https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/2025-minimum-elements-software-bill-materials-sbom ; https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03183/BSI-TR-03183-2_v2_1_0.html ; https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/06/27/2025-11669/ ; https://www.insidegovernmentcontracts.com/2026/02/omb-rescinds-the-common-form-secure-software-attestation-requirement/ ; https://github.com/interlynk-io/sbomqs ; https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0829_002.html ; https://standards.iteh.ai/catalog/standards/cen/487254bf-baa1-48e9-be33-658b37f6fb90/pren-40000-1-3 ; https://docs.oasis-open.org/csaf/csaf/v2.1/csaf-v2.1.html
strengths: 16 compliance levels with a single StandardChecker dispatch (src/quality/compliance/context.rs) and a typed rule registry (registry.rs, ~129 RuleMeta entries) that maps every violation to harmonised-standard clause IDs (CRA articles/annexes, prEN 40000-1-3 PRE-7-RQ-xx, BSI sections, SSDF practices) plus remediation text — stronger cross-referencing than sbomqs or ntia-conformance-checker offer.

EU CRA depth is ahead of the market: phase-aware profiles, Art. 24 OSS-steward light profile, Annex III/IV product-class severity calibration (mod.rs class_severity), Annex VIII conformity-route evidence checklists, and a sidecar mechanism (--cra-sidecar) for manufacturer metadata SBOMs cannot carry.

Crypto/PQC coverage (CNSA 2.0, NIST IR 8547/FIPS 203-205 over CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM cryptoProperties) with the recent fix removing vacuous passes (17ae0b0) is a genuine differentiator; almost no comparable OSS tool checks CNSA 2.0 against a CBOM.
AI-BOM profiles (EU AI Act Annex IV readiness, BSI/G7 SBOM-for-AI minimum elements) with honest N/A guards for non-AI SBOMs and explicit readiness-not-conformity framing.

NormalizedSbom already carries nearly all data needed for the missing profiles: per-component hashes, LicenseInfo, Creator/Tool, lifecycle_phase, completeness_declaration, SignatureInfo, supplier, is_external, vulnerabilities/VEX, support_end_date, EolInfo — so most gaps are rule-authoring, not model surgery.

confirmed.title: BSI TR-03183-2 profile validates against superseded v2.0.0 and never enforces the mandatory SBOM format/version gate
confirmed.description: The checker documents itself as 'Reference: BSI TR-03183-2 v2.0.0 §5/§6'. BSI published v2.1.0 on 2025-08-20 (https://www.bsi.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/EN/BSI/Publications/TechGuidelines/TR03183/BSI-TR-03183-2_v2_1_0.html), which raises the required formats to CycloneDX >= 1.6 or SPDX >= 3.0.1 (other formats/versions are non-compliant) and reorganizes fields into Required/Additional/Optional. bsi.rs contains no check on sbom.document.format/spec_version at all — not even the v2.0.0 floor (CycloneDX 1.5 / SPDX 2.2.1) — so format eligibility is silently skipped. Competing tooling (sbomqs) already exposes bsi-v2.0 and v2.1 feature profiles.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A vendor runs `sbom-tools validate sbom.json --standard bsi` on a CycloneDX 1.4 SBOM that carries author/timestamp/hashes/licenses. sbom-tools reports the BSI profile as compliant; under the current TR-03183-2 v2.1.0 (and even v2.0.0's format clause) the document is non-conformant purely on format version, and a German-market/CRA audit citing TR-03183 rejects it.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED. bsi.rs check_bsi_tr_03183_2 (the only code run for ComplianceLevel::BsiTr03183_2 per context.rs:148 dispatch) contains no check on sbom.document.format or spec_version; registry.rs BSI rules (738-768) cover only §5.1-5.5/§6 with no format rule; mod.rs check() adds no format gate; none of the four recent fix commits address this. The CLI path exists (validate.rs:97-98 maps --standard bsi to this checker) and the parser accepts CycloneDX 1.4 (cyclonedx.rs:1165), so a CDX 1.4 SBOM with author/timestamp/hashes/PURLs/deps is reported BSI-compliant despite failing TR-03183-2's mandatory f

confirmed.title: FDA profile predates the June 27, 2025 final premarket cybersecurity guidance (supersedes Sept 2023; SBOM statutory under FD&C §524B(b)(3))
confirmed.description: StandardKind::FdaPremarket's canonical URL points at the fda.gov guidance landing page (which now hosts the 2025 final), but all FDA rules in registry.rs (lines ~520-590) carry only the versionless ref '(FdaPremarket, "FDA Premarket")' and the checks in generic.rs were written to the 2023 edition. The June 2025 final (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/06/27/2025-11669/) supersedes the 2023 guidance, adds Section VII implementing FD&C §524B for 'cyber devices' (SBOM is a statutory requirement, not a recommendation), and explicitly expects machine-readability plus per-component level-of-support and end-of-support dates. Several FDA checks still use 'should' phrasing and Warning severity (e.g. SBOM-FDA-SUPPORT Warning for missing support/contact info) where the 2025 guidance is mandatory for cyber devices.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer preparing a 510(k) premarket submission in 2026 validates with --standard fda; sbom-tools passes an SBOM lacking per-component end-of-support dates (only a Warning), but FDA reviewers applying the June 2025 final guidance and §524B(b)(3) issue a deficiency letter for the same SBOM.

confirmed.title: BSI/G7 SBOM-for-AI profile may lag the jointly-published CISA/G7 final (May 12, 2026) and its canonical help URI is a bare domain root
confirmed.description: The profile is pinned to the 'BSI/G7 (Feb 2026)' edition (bsi_sbom_for_ai.rs module header) and canonical_help_uri returns the unstable root 'https://www.bsi.bund.de' rather than a document URL. CISA and G7 partners published the joint 'Software Bill of Materials for AI — Minimum Elements' on May 12, 2026 (https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/software-bill-materials-ai-minimum-elements), which is the citable final; element wording/clustering should be re-verified against it and the StandardRef URI pointed at a stable resource page.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user clicks the help_uri from a SARIF finding for SBOM-BSIAI-MODEL and lands on the BSI homepage with no path to the guidance; a GRC reviewer cross-checking against the May 2026 CISA/G7 publication finds the tool cites a pre-final BSI edition and questions the mapping.

improvements.title: Add a CISA 2025 SBOM Minimum Elements profile (successor to NTIA 2021)
improvements.description: CISA's '2025 Minimum Elements for a SBOM' (draft Aug 2025, comment period closed 2025-10-03; produced under OMB M-22-18 as the designated NTIA successor — https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/2025-minimum-elements-software-bill-materials-sbom) adds Component Hash, License, Tool Name, and Generation Context to the 2021 elements and tightens author/producer/version definitions. sbomqs already ships an 'ntia-2025' profile, so buyers comparing tools will notice the absence. NormalizedSbom already carries everything needed: Component.hashes, LicenseInfo, Creator{creator_type: Tool}, and DocumentMetadata.lifecycle_phase (generation context). Implement as a new ComplianceLevel (e.g. Cisa2025) layered on the existing NTIA checks in generic.rs + ~6 new registry rules; keep NtiaMinimum as-is for legacy contracts and re-verify wording when CISA publishes the final.

improvements.title: Add a PCI DSS 4.0 Requirement 6.3.2 software-inventory profile
improvements.description: PCI DSS 4.0 §6.3.2 (inventory of bespoke/custom software and all embedded third-party components, maintained and *used* for vulnerability management) moved from best-practice to mandatory on 2025-03-31; QSAs now accept SBOMs as the canonical evidence, and Sonatype/Interlynk/FOSSA all market §6.3.2 support (https://fossa.com/blog/understanding-sbom-requirements-pci-dss/). Checks map directly onto existing data: component completeness (completeness_declaration), third-party identification (supplier / is_external / ecosystem), name+version present, and vulnerability-management usability (Component.vulnerabilities / VulnerabilityRef presence or external VDR ref). Also cover companion control 11.3.1.1. This is largely re-badging existing generic checks under PCI-referenced rule IDs with a StandardKind::PciDss4 registry entry.

improvements.title: Ingest machine-readable attestation evidence: in-toto attestation bundles and CycloneDX Attestations (CDXA)
improvements.description: Today conformity evidence is detected only as an ExternalRefType::Attestation/Certification presence bit (cra.rs lines 41-94, 637-676) — the engine cannot open an in-toto statement (SLSA provenance predicate) or a CycloneDX CDXA declarations/claims/evidence document and verify that a claimed standard requirement is actually attested. CDXA explicitly models 'standards' with requirement taxonomies (CRA, SSDF) and cdxgen now emits signed CDXA documents (https://github.com/cyclonedx/specification). Consuming these would upgrade the CRA Annex VIII route checklists (Module B+C/H currently satisfied by ANY attestation external ref, regardless of content) and the SSDF profile (PS/PW/RV practices could be evidenced by SLSA provenance instead of heuristics on VCS refs). Suggested phasing: (1) parse CDXA and map claims to registry rule IDs, (2) accept in-toto/SLSA provenance as evidence for SSDF PS.1/PS.2/PS.3 and EO 14028 auto-generation, (3) signature verification via sigstore as an optional feature.

improvements.title: Track BSI TR-03183-2 v2.1.0 and add the format-eligibility gate (upgrade path for the drift finding)
improvements.description: Concrete upgrade for the version-drift finding: add a format/spec-version check (CycloneDX >= 1.6 or SPDX >= 3.0.1 per v2.1.0; document v2.0.0 floor as a lenient mode), reorganize rule severities to the v2.1.0 Required/Additional/Optional categories, and version the StandardRef IDs (e.g. 'TR-03183-2 v2.1 §5.2') so auditors know which edition was checked. The parser side already supports CycloneDX 1.6/1.7 and SPDX 3.0 per docs/standards-support-plan.md, so DocumentMetadata.spec_version is available to gate on.

improvements.title: Add CISA 'Framing Software Component Transparency' (3rd ed., 2024) attribute-maturity profile
improvements.description: CISA's 2024 Framing document defines SBOM attributes in three maturity tiers (Minimum Expected / Recommended Practice / Aspirational Goal) and is the reference sbomqs implements as its 'fsct' profile. A tiered scorecard (rather than pass/fail) fits the existing quality-score machinery in src/quality and would give users a maturity ladder between NtiaMinimum and Comprehensive. All required attributes (component hash, license, copyright holder, dependency completeness declarations) already exist on Component/DocumentMetadata.

improvements.title: Add Japan METI SBOM Guide v2.0 (Aug 2024) profile
improvements.description: METI's 'Guide of Introduction of SBOM for Software Management ver. 2.0' (2024-08-29, https://www.meti.go.jp/english/press/2024/0829_002.html) is the reference for Japanese procurement (notably medical-device and automotive sectors) and is NTIA-aligned with added vulnerability-management-process expectations; Japan also co-signed the shared-vision SBOM guidance in Sept 2025. Effort is small — largely a re-badged NTIA/vuln-usability rule set with METI section references — and it opens APAC positioning no comparable Rust tool covers.

improvements.title: Add OpenChain Telco SBOM Guide v1.1 profile and ISO 5230/18974 evidence mapping
improvements.description: The OpenChain Telco SBOM Guide v1.1 (SPDX-based field requirements for telecom procurement) is covered by sbomqs as 'oct-v1.1'; checks are a small superset of existing NTIA+BSI field rules (SPDX-specific: creator comment with SPDX version, PackageSupplier, PackageChecksum). Separately, OpenChain ISO/IEC 5230 (license compliance) and ISO/IEC 18974 (security assurance) are process standards — full conformance is out of scope for a document checker, but an 'evidence readiness' mapping (concluded vs declared licenses populated, license texts referenced, vulnerability-response contact present) would let OpenChain-certified suppliers use sbom-tools output as program evidence. LicenseInfo and security_contact fields already exist.

improvements.title: sbomqs/BSI scoring interoperability profile (comparable per-standard 0-10 scores)
improvements.description: The quality engine scores 0-100 with its own profiles (minimal/standard/security/license-compliance/cra/comprehensive/cbom) while the de-facto interop baseline is sbomqs' 0-10 per-feature scoring with named profiles (ntia, ntia-2025, fsct, bsi-v1.1/v2.0/v2.1, oct-v1.1). Emitting an sbomqs-comparable score block (feature name -> score) per compliance level, or documenting a mapping, would let users mix sbom-tools into pipelines/dashboards (e.g. Dependency-Track ingestion of sbomqs scores) without renormalizing. This is presentation-layer work on top of existing check results.

improvements.title: SSDF-attestation evidence mapping for the (now risk-based) US federal procurement flow
improvements.description: OMB M-26-05 (2026-01-23) rescinded the mandatory CISA Secure Software Development Attestation Common Form from M-22-18/M-23-16, but explicitly allows agencies to keep using the form and to contractually require 'a current SBOM upon request' (https://www.insidegovernmentcontracts.com/2026/02/omb-rescinds-the-common-form-secure-software-attestation-requirement/). A low-cost win: a report mode that maps the existing NistSsdf/Eo14028 check results onto the Common Form's four practice areas so vendors can attach sbom-tools output as attestation evidence. Framing matters post-M-26-05: sell it as evidence support, not a compliance mandate. FedRAMP similarly consumes SSDF-aligned evidence rather than defining its own SBOM profile.

improvements.title: NIST SP 800-161r1 C-SCRM control mapping (SR-3/SR-4/RA-9)
improvements.description: SP 800-161r1 (incl. the Appendix F EO 14028 guidance) references SBOM as evidence for supply-chain controls SR-3 (supply chain controls/processes), SR-4 (provenance), and RA-9 (criticality analysis). Federal integrators and their primes map deliverables to 800-161 controls in GRC systems; adding (K::NistScrm, "SR-4") style refs to existing provenance/supplier/hash rules in registry.rs (same pattern as the prEN cross-references) would make sbom-tools SARIF ingest cleanly into those systems without any new checks.

improvements.title: Standards-watch items: EN 40000-1-3 finalization, CSAF 2.1, CISA 2025 final, NIST IR 8547 final
improvements.description: Four pinned references will move within ~12 months and should be tracked (a STANDARDS_VERSIONS.md or registry-level version tags would formalize this): (1) prEN 40000-1-3 passed public enquiry and is under approval with delivery expected Aug 2026 — the PRE-7-RQ-xx IDs hardcoded in registry.rs may renumber at publication (mod.rs line 375 already anticipates this via CRA-P5.1); (2) CSAF 2.1 reached OASIS CSD02 on 2026-02-25 (https://docs.oasis-open.org/csaf/csaf/v2.1/csaf-v2.1.html) — StandardKind::Csaf2 ('CSAF v2.0 / ISO/IEC 20153:2025') stays correct until 2.1 becomes an OASIS Standard; (3) CISA 2025 Minimum Elements final will supersede the draft the proposed Cisa2025 profile would target; (4) NIST IR 8547 is still the Nov 2024 initial public draft — the NistPqc description citing it is fine today but the final may shift deprecation dates (RSA-2048/P-256 deprecated 2030, disallowed 2035).

missed: TUI compliance surface (~4,075 LOC across 8 files) audited by no area: src/tui/shared/compliance.rs, src/tui/view/views/compliance.rs (1,274 LOC), src/tui/view/views/pqc_compliance.rs, src/tui/view/views/algorithms.rs, src/tui/views/diff_compliance.rs (1,401 LOC), src/tui/app_states/compliance.rs, src/tui/view_states/compliance.rs, src/tui/events/compliance.rs. Spot-check found real verdict-display defects: (a) src/tui/view/views/pqc_compliance.rs:159-169 maps per-algorithm NIST PQC status as Error->FAIL, Info->OK, everything else -> green PASS, so a Warning-severity PQC violation renders as PASS (wrong verdict on screen); (b) pqc_compliance.rs:148-156 derives per-row CNSA2/PQC verdicts from absence of a violation with v.element == comp.name, so document-level violations (element=None) never attach to any row, same-named components conflate, and combined with area 4's confirmed CNSA2 false-pass surfaces the README-advertised (README.md:53) 'per-algorithm PASS/FAIL assessment' prints an affirmative green PASS for e.g. RSA-2048 in a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM — the TUI amplifies the engine's silent false-pass into an explicit endorsement.

TUI compliance export path src/tui/export.rs:260-520 unaudited: compliance_to_json (:333) is a second, hand-rolled machine-readable JSON contract whose shape diverges from the serde ComplianceResult JSON (Debug-formatted severity strings, category.name(), no rule_id/standard_refs), plus hand-rolled markdown (:383), CSV (:426 — a compliance export format the CLI does not offer at all), and HTML (:454). Only SARIF delegates to reports::sarif (:374).

Two more copies of the confirmed Info-inflation compliance score formula: area 6 flagged only src/cli/validate.rs:205-212, but the identical formula (total = violations.len()+1; issues = errors+warnings; Info raises total but not issues, inflating the score) is duplicated at src/reports/markdown.rs:777-786 (compliance_score) and src/reports/html.rs:629 (compliance_score_html), used by diff/view CRA report sections. Fixing validate.rs alone leaves the same defect in HTML/markdown reports.
